answer:
Use Quantum ESPRESSO for the variable-cell relaxation and subsequent SCF calculation.
Use the LDA pseudopotentials PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/bi.upf, PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/fe.upf, and PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/o.upf.
Start from an R3c primitive cell consistent with BiFeO3 perovskite with 10 atoms per cell.
Use rhombohedral lattice vectors with a = 5.63 Angstrom and alpha = 59.4 degrees.
Set the primitive-cell atomic coordinates as Bi at (0.000, 0.000, 0.000), Fe at (0.221, 0.221, 0.221), and O at (0.538, 0.933, 0.387) in fractional coordinates.
Define the 10-atom cell by including the two Bi, two Fe, and six O positions generated by the R3c symmetry operations of the primitive cell.
Run a spin-unpolarized calculation with no Hubbard U and no spin-orbit coupling.
Set ecutwfc = 70 Ry and ecutrho = 280 Ry.
Set etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8.
Use an automatic Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid of 8x8x8 with a half shift specified as 1 1 1.
First perform a variable-cell relaxation, allowing both the cell parameters and atomic positions to relax.
After the vc-relax converges, take the fully relaxed structure as the new input geometry.
Run a self-consistent field calculation on the relaxed structure using the same ecutwfc, ecutrho, k-point grid, pseudopotentials, and functional settings.
Report the fully relaxed lattice vectors, relaxed atomic positions, and the final total energy from the SCF calculation.
